instructions: Put the 1 1/2 cups rice in a bowl, cover it with cold water, swish it with your hand and pour the water off. Do this 3 or 4 times, until the water is only a little cloudy, then drain the rice well in a sieve.
Put the rice in a rice cooker or a heavy pot with 1 1/2 cups cold water and let it soak for 20 minutes.

Cook the rice. In a rice cooker, start it now. In a pot, bring it to a boil over high, cover it, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 13 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir the 4 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt together in a small bowl. Microwave it for 30 seconds and stir until the sugar and salt have dissolved. Set it aside to cool.
Gently squeeze each of the 12 inari age pouches over a small bowl to catch the sweet liquid, and set the pouches on a plate.
Wet a large baking sheet or a wide bowl and shake off the extra water. Spread the hot rice over it with a rice paddle or a flat spatula.
Drizzle the vinegar mix over the rice. Cut through the rice with the edge of the paddle and turn it over gently, working your way across. Don't stir it, or the grains break and turn mushy.

Keep cutting and turning for about 5 minutes, fanning the rice with a plate or a piece of cardboard as you go, until it's about as warm as your skin. Sprinkle over the 1 tbsp sesame seeds and fold them through the same way.
Divide the rice into 12 portions of about 1/4 cup. Dip your fingers in the pouch liquid and press each portion gently into an oval. Press only enough to hold it together.
Open a pouch with your fingertips, easing it apart all the way into the corners. The skin is thin, so go slowly. Fold the top edge back a little, like a cuff.

Slide a rice oval into the pouch and push it gently into the corners. Unfold the cuff and fold the edges over the rice like you're wrapping a present. Set it seam side down and fill the rest of the pouches the same way.
Serve at room temperature. To pack them for lunch, fit them snugly in a container, keep them cool and eat them the same day. The rice turns hard in the fridge.
method_notes: All three fill fried tofu pouches with warm sushi rice seasoned with rice vinegar, sugar and salt, and Just One Cookbook and RecipeTin Japan fold toasted sesame seeds through it. Just One Cookbook cooks the rice with equal parts water so it stays firm enough to take the vinegar, and uses store-bought seasoned pouches, wetting your hands with their liquid before shaping. RecipeTin Japan and Hungry Huy simmer plain aburaage themselves for about 10 minutes, RecipeTin Japan in dashi, soy sauce, sake, mirin and sugar and Hungry Huy in dashi, soy sauce, sugar and miso. This one follows the lead and uses store-bought pouches to keep it a weekday lunch.
